items.title: Context
items.body:
SpecPad reads and writes files under `docs/specpad/` in a git repository. There is no database.

| Outside the software | Reached by |
|---|---|
| A git repository | The `git` binary, for history and publication |
| A local checkout | The browser's File System Access API |
| A SpecPad server | HTTP, when the user has no checkout of their own |
| Claude Code | The skill, which edits the same files programmatically |
| An eQMS | Exported evidence; outside the scope of this software |

Any actor that can read and write the JSON and markdown under `docs/specpad/` is a full client. The
files are the interface.

items.title: Composition
items.body:
| Block | Units |
|---|---|
| Shared contract | schema, docTypes, validate, governance, ids, factories, diff, merge, verification, launcher |
| Editor shell | LocalApp, fileApi, transports (local/demo/remote), launchParams, theme, handleStore |
| Editor views | register tables, TestingView, ArchitectureView, DetailedDesignView, JobsView, ReleasesView, Auditor, Traceability, Overview, chrome |
| Editor derivations | changeTracking, archDiff, auditReport, designControls, outline |
| Server | config, registry, routing, auth, paths, git, repository, workingCopy, commitGate, api, entry point, presence, events, branchWatcher |
| Skill | SKILL.md procedures, templates, verification adapter, mirror sync |

Units are grouped by what changes together rather than by directory. `fileApi` is grouped with the
shell rather than the transports because it owns file conventions, which change with the document set.

items.title: Dependency
items.body:
The editor and the server both depend on `src/shared`. `src/shared` depends on nothing in `src/`,
`server/` or `site/`.

The skill mirrors the contract in prose and is held to it by `skill/__tests__/parity.test.ts`; it is a
prompt, not a program, so it cannot import. `server/__tests__/contract-parity.test.ts` asserts the
server declares no copy of validation, governance, merge or diff.

items.title: Information model
items.body:
Every document carries `schemaVersion`, `type`, `name` and `title`. Register documents add an
ordered `items[]`. Each item has a stable `id` and an optional renameable `code`.

References target ids: `verifies` → SRS, `satisfies` → PRD, `design` → SDD.

Three things are not stored:

- **History** — no author, no modified date, no change counter. Git holds this.
- **Derived values** — test counts, result roll-ups, release-to-job mapping and coverage are computed
  on read.
- **Reverse links** — each trace edge is authored in one place and reversed at render time.

The caches under `.specpad/` hold verbatim copies of past versions of these same files. They contain
no derived data and are rebuildable from git.

items.title: External interfaces
items.body:
**`FileApi`** (`src/transports/types.ts`) — `listDocuments`, `readJson`, `readText`,
`writeText`. An absent file returns `null`; an unreadable path also returns `null`, so one
unresolvable diagram reference cannot abort opening a project. All three transports pass one
conformance suite.

**HTTP API** (`/api/v1/…`, optionally under `/p/<project>`) — the same operations plus session,
status, commit, discard, presence and events. A refused commit returns 409 with the gate result or the
conflicts as the body; it is data the dialog renders, not an error.

**Git** — every command goes through an injectable runner.

**Server-sent events** — advisory presence and an upstream-moved signal.

items.title: Conventions used throughout
items.body:
- Ids are generated once and never change: a typed prefix and six hex digits (`r_`, `t_`, `p_`,
  `d_`, `h_`, `j_`), unique within a file, issued only by `ids.ts`.
- Codes are labels. Nothing resolves by code, so renaming one is always safe.
- Governance rules that depend on an optional register run only when that register is present.
- Presence, the branch watcher and project discovery degrade to silence on failure.
- Absent, refused and broken are three distinct results.

items.title: Degradation and failure behaviour
items.body:
| Missing | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| File System Access API | Upload/download fallback; in server mode the API is used instead |
| `EventSource` | Presence subscription becomes a no-op |
| A server | The session probe requires JSON *and* a session shape, so a static host answering an unknown path with `index.html` is not mistaken for one |
| A referenced diagram | The project opens; that diagram renders as missing |
| One project's repository | The other projects on the server still serve |

Each degraded path has a test asserting the degraded behaviour rather than the absence of a crash.

items.title: schema — types and JSON Schemas
items.body:
TypeScript types and JSON Schemas for every document type, defined together so they cannot drift.

Exports `projectSchema`, `srsSchema`, `vtpSchema`, `prdSchema`, `sddSchema`, the matching types,
and `SCHEMA_VERSION`.

Structure only. Whether a reference resolves is governance's concern. Every property carries a
description, which `schema-descriptions.test.ts` enforces, because the published schema reference is
generated from them.

items.title: docTypes — the document-type registry
items.body:
The registry of content document types, and how each behaves: `register` | `prose` | `asset`,
optional, in-baseline, generated.

Exports `DOC_TYPES`, `REGISTER_TYPES`, `docTypeFor`, `isRegisterType`, `registerTypesInIndex`.
An unknown type returns `undefined`.

Validation, the schema reference, snapshots, per-job diffs, the redline and the generator all iterate
the registry, so a new pillar is a registration plus a schema. Adding the SDD (JOB-44) changed no
snapshot, diff or generator code.

items.title: validate — structural validation
items.body:
`validate(doc)` returns an array of problems; empty means structurally valid. It reports every
problem rather than stopping at the first.

Says nothing about policy: a document can be structurally valid and violate traceability.

items.title: governance — policy
items.body:
The rules that make a document set trustworthy, as opposed to well-formed.

`GOVERNANCE_RULES` is the canonical list. `checkGovernance(bundle)` returns violations, and is pure
over data — which is why the editor, the skill and the server can all run it without disagreeing.

| Rule | Applies |
|---|---|
| `traceability` | Always |
| `referential-integrity` | Always |
| `missing-expected` | Always |
| `active-job-open`, `active-job-known` | When a jobs register exists |
| `prd-referential-integrity`, `prd-coverage` | When a PRD register is present |
| `sdd-referential-integrity`, `sdd-coverage` | When a detailed design is present |

Rules requiring `HEAD` — "spec changes require an active job" — live in the skill's pre-commit gate,
because a browser has no git.

`sdd-coverage` is checked at full rigour with no configuration to relax it. IEC 62304 makes the
per-unit design Class C only and FDA submits the SDS only at Enhanced; omission is an export decision,
so no safety class or documentation level appears in the contract.

items.title: ids — identity
items.body:
`generateId(prefix, existing)` returns a typed prefix plus six hex digits, retrying on collision with
the supplied set and giving up after a bounded number of attempts.

Ids are random rather than sequential: two people adding items offline must not mint the same id, and a
counter would be state to store and merge.

items.title: factories — new documents and items
items.body:
Constructors for empty documents and new items. `createProjectDoc` builds `documents[]` from
`REGISTER_TYPES`, so a newly registered pillar joins the default document set without changing this
unit.

items.title: diff — item-level comparison
items.body:
`diffItems(before, after)` returns added, removed and modified items, matched by `id`. Item order is
not compared.

`valuesEqual` is exported and used by the redline, the merge and the pending-change summary, so
"changed" means the same thing in all three.

items.title: merge — three-way structural merge
items.body:
`mergeDocs(base, ours, theirs)` returns the merged document and a list of conflicts. Pure; performs
no I/O.

Items are matched by `id`. Field-level changes from both sides are combined. A conflict is reported
when both sides set the same field to different values, or one side deletes an item the other
modified. Item order is not compared. A document with no `items[]` array is rejected.

Documents are never merged as text: a line-based merge of a formatted JSON array can produce duplicated
ids, references to deleted items, and dropped items, none of which are visible in a diff review.

items.title: verification — run matching
items.body:
Resolves a VTP item's `automation` links against a captured run and derives its result.

`runner` and `selector` are opaque strings, so the contract is independent of any test framework.
Automated tests derive `passed`, `failed`, `skipped` or `not_run`; manual tests fall back to their
stored `result`. Roll-ups are computed, not stored.

A selector may name a single test or a group of them. A result answers a selector when its name
equals it or begins with it at a word boundary, so a link naming a `describe` block resolves to every
test beneath it, and adding a test to that group needs no change to the verification plan. The
boundary check prevents a selector matching a longer name it merely prefixes.

A group is `failed` if any test beneath it failed, and `skipped` only if all of them were.

A link with no matching result is `not_run`, which is distinct from `failed`.

items.title: launcher — where the editor lives
items.body:
`editorVersionPath` maps a contract version to an editor build path: `"1.0"` → `/v01/`. The path is
derived, never configured. A `schemaVersion` with no numeric major throws.

`editorUrl(base)` falls back to the public hosted editor when `base` is blank or absent. The server
imports this rather than deriving its own copy.

items.title: LocalApp — the editor shell
items.body:
The editor root. Owns the open project, the active view, the loaded document set, and the derived state
the views read.

On load it resolves how this session reaches its files, in order:

1. A SpecPad server serving the page (probe `/api/v1/session`, under `/p/<id>` when the URL names a
   project).
2. The hosted demo, when the URL carries `?demo`.
3. Local files.

It is the only unit that decides where documents come from; no view knows.

`sessionReadOnly` is the single condition governing whether any view offers an editing affordance. It
is true only when a server role forbids writing. The demo is not read-only: it is a sandbox whose edits
are held in memory and offered as a download.

A project that cannot be opened sets an error and leaves the editor closed rather than half-loaded.

items.title: fileApi — document conventions
items.body:
Owns SpecPad's file conventions — which filename holds which document, where a snapshot lives, what
"absent" means for an optional sidecar — and delegates all I/O to the active `FileApi`.

This separation is why adding a transport changed no view, and adding a document type changed no
transport.

items.title: local transport — File System Access
items.body:
Reads and writes a local checkout through the File System Access API, including permission re-prompting
and the upload/download fallback where the API is unavailable.

A revoked or stale directory handle reports as not-open rather than throwing on first read, so the
editor can offer to re-pick the folder.

items.title: demo transport — read-only hosted content
items.body:
Reads the hosted demo's static files over HTTP from a manifest. Every write is refused with a message
naming the demo.

The editor no longer treats demo mode as read-only — the sandbox holds edits in memory and never calls
`writeText` — so this refusal is a backstop rather than the behaviour a user meets.

items.title: remote transport — a SpecPad server
items.body:
The `FileApi` implementation for a SpecPad server, plus session, status, commit, discard, presence,
events and project discovery.

The API base carries the project (`/api/v1/p/<id>`), so one transport serves single-project and
multi-project deployments. `fetchProjects` always queries the deployment root, since the project list
describes the server rather than the open project.

Version tags seen on read are replayed on write. A write built on a superseded version is refused by
the server rather than overwriting.

Status codes are not interchangeable:

| Code | Meaning | Returned as |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | Absent | `null` |
| 400 (text read) | Unresolvable path | `null` |
| 409 (commit) | Refused, with the gate result or conflicts | the payload, for rendering |
| other | Error | throws `RemoteError` |

Conflating 404 and 409 returned the error body in place of the document.

items.title: launchParams — reading the launch URL
items.body:
Parses the launch URL. `name`, `open` and `dir` are read from the fragment, which browsers do not
send to a server, so a local folder path stays local. `demo` and `project` are read from the query
string, and from the fragment as a fallback.

An unrecognised `open` value is ignored.

items.title: theme — appearance
items.body:
Themes are CSS custom properties under `[data-theme]`, so a new theme is a block of variables. The
stored theme is applied pre-paint by an inline script in `index.html`; an unknown stored value falls
back to the default.

items.title: handleStore — recent projects
items.body:
Persists directory handles in IndexedDB so a return visit can reopen a project without a picker.
Unsupported browsers get an empty list. A handle whose permission grant has lapsed is reported for
re-picking.

items.title: changeTracking — redline and attribution
items.body:
`buildRedline` computes a redline from two document versions; `computeAttribution` assembles
per-item attribution from an ordered sequence of snapshots. Both are pure over documents.

The snapshots are the committed verbatim copies under `.specpad/`, so the browser needs no git and no
diff is stored. A missing snapshot yields no redline rather than an empty one, keeping "unchanged"
distinct from "unknown".

items.title: archDiff — section-level markdown diff
items.body:
`mdSectionDiff(before, after)` reports which heading sections of a markdown document changed.

Diagrams are compared coarsely — changed or not. No regulator tracks in-diagram deltas, and semantic
diagram comparison is unsolved.

items.title: auditReport — coverage and roll-ups
items.body:
`buildAuditReport(docs, run)` computes coverage, the trace matrix and test roll-ups.

Automated results are derived from the run rather than from a stored field, which is why the run is a
parameter. Roll-ups broke when stored results were cleared in favour of captured ones; threading the
run through fixed it.

items.title: designControls — the regulatory map
items.body:
`buildDesignControls(input)` returns the formal design-control elements, each with IEC 62304 and
21 CFR 820.30 citations, a plain statement, a status of present, partial or gap, and the tab holding
its evidence.

Design Outputs covers 62304 §5.3 and §5.4 together: partial with the architecture or the detailed
design alone, present only with both. A detailed design with no sections does not count. Status is
derived on read, so it cannot claim evidence that is no longer present.

The citations are in core rather than the medical add-on: "where are your design inputs?" must be
answerable in any project.

items.title: outline — heading hierarchy
items.body:
Renders a flat `items[]` with `level` as a numbered hierarchy, composing each heading's dotted code
from its ancestors. Items stay flat in storage; the tree exists only at render time.

items.title: Register tables — SRS, VTP, PRD
items.body:
Inline editing for an id-keyed register: click a cell to edit, row menu for structure, expandable
reference cells, redline decoration, presence markers.

Three tables rather than one generic component. Each register has a different set of columns that
matter, and the abstraction covering all three was worse than the duplication.

Expanding a requirement row shows its whole trace — satisfies, design, verifies — with the first two edited through `RefPicker`. The edges are stored on the item the row shows.

With `readOnly`, no row menu renders, no cell opens for editing, and the pickers offer no controls.

items.title: RefPicker — choosing a reference
items.body:
Selects the items a trace edge points at.

Every edge stores ids (`verifies`, `satisfies`, `design`) while a human works in codes and text. The picker shows each candidate's code and text, filters on both, and stores its id; no identifier is typed or displayed for a reference that resolves.

Headings are not offered as candidates. A reference that does not resolve is displayed as unresolved and can be removed, rather than being hidden or dropped — discarding it silently would conceal the breakage governance reports.

items.title: TestingView — the evidence chain
items.body:
Presents the chain **VTP item → automated test → captured run**, with run provenance.

Automated rows show a derived status and no result control; manual rows keep one. A derived value is
not editable, or a failing run could be typed over.

items.title: ArchitectureView — authoring and display
items.body:
Edit and Display sub-views for the arc42 markdown. Display renders with react-markdown, resolving each
`![alt](name.svg)` from the loaded diagram map. Edit is a CodeMirror markdown editor. Diagrams are
authored externally in draw.io.

An unresolvable diagram reference renders as missing and does not abort opening the project.

items.title: JobsView — change tracking
items.body:
A job's impact: per-document-type diffs from the frozen caches, architecture changes, commits, and the
verification roll-up. For the active job it diffs the before-snapshot against the working copy, so
uncommitted work is visible before the job closes.

Iterates the registered document types, so a new pillar's changes appear without an edit here.

items.title: ReleasesView — release notes
items.body: Release notes per release, newest first. A release's job list is derived from each job's `version`.

items.title: Auditor and Traceability views
items.body:
Two views. The Auditor is orientation: the design-control map, which formal element lives where. The
Traceability view is evidence: the matrix, coverage and gaps.

They were one view. A reviewer arriving cold needs the map before the matrix.

Both render a scope disclaimer: this is evidence supporting design controls, not a quality system.

items.title: OverviewView — the landing view
items.body:
Coverage headline, in-progress jobs, latest release, quick jumps. All derived on read; absent pillars
are omitted rather than shown empty.

items.title: Editor chrome — menubar, tabs, status, server bar, dialogs
items.body:
The menu bar, tab strip, status bar, server bar and Commit dialog.

Document tabs are labelled by acronym (PRD, SRS, SAD, SDD, VTP) with the full name as hover text. The
tab strip is a CSS grid so a phase band can span several tabs; Design Outputs spans the SAD and SDD.

The server bar reports identity, role, unpublished count and current project. The Commit dialog shows
the pending change set at item level and the governance result before anything is committed, and
renders refusals and per-field conflicts rather than discarding them.

In the demo the Save control becomes Download and hands back the JSON. Row menus render in a portal so
they are not clipped by the table.

items.title: DetailedDesignView — the design tab
items.body:
The detailed design, rendered as one continuous document with a sticky outline.

- The document column stacks every section in order — group headings, then each section's
  `code · title`, source paths, the requirements implementing it, and its rendered body.
- The outline tracks the section in view (IntersectionObserver) and scrolls to a section on click.
- Editing is in place: selecting a section's body replaces it with a CodeMirror editor between its
  neighbours. There is no document-level edit mode.
- Each section header carries a menu: add below, add group, move up, move down, delete.
- Outline entries reorder by drag, using `@dnd-kit`.

Section boundaries are data, not formatting. `SrsItem.design` points at a section id, so a continuous
rendering changes presentation only. A `##` inside a body is sub-structure within that section and
cannot be traced to.

Each section lists the requirements referencing it, and can add or remove them. The edge is stored on the requirement, so this writes to the SRS document through `onChangeSrs` — one home per edge, reachable from either end.

Editing a section states that the referencing requirements are now in question; deleting one names the references that would be left unresolved.

items.title: server/config — the deployment declaration
items.body:
The deployment declaration: projects, identity, roles, commit policy, working-copy lifecycle.

`validateConfig` collects every problem; `loadConfig` throws with all of them. A server holding push
access to a real repository does not start half-configured.

A project entry carries its own repository, branch, allowlisted paths and credential, and may override
the server-wide role map and commit policy. The single-repository shape (`repo: {…}` at the root) is
read as a one-project deployment.

`workingCopies.idleTimeout` defaults to 24 hours; `0` disables reaping.

items.title: server/registry — the hosted projects
items.body:
Holds one runtime per project: a `Repository`, a `PresenceRegistry`, an `EventBus` and a
`BranchWatcher`. Presence and the upstream signal are meaningful only within a project.

`ensureClones` returns failures rather than throwing, so one unreachable repository does not prevent
the others being served.

items.title: server/routing — which project a request is for
items.body:
`parseApiPath` splits `/p/<id>/…` into a project id and the remaining path. Pure string functions,
testable without a server or a clone.

A path naming no project resolves only when the deployment has exactly one. An unknown project is a
404; an unnamed project on a multi-project server is a 400 carrying the list of projects the caller may
open.

items.title: server/auth — identity and authorization
items.body:
SpecPad implements no authentication. A provider normalises an identity asserted elsewhere into a
`Principal`, and nothing downstream knows which provider produced it.

| Provider | Source of identity |
|---|---|
| `proxy` | Headers from a trusted upstream (oauth2-proxy, Entra App Proxy, Cloudflare Access) |
| `dev` | A fixed identity, loopback binds only |
| `oidc` | Not implemented; throws with instructions to use `proxy` |

Identity is not the git credential. The authenticated user is the commit **author**; the push uses a
machine credential configured by the operator.

Authentication is deployment-wide and authorization is per project, so they are separate steps:
`authenticate` then `sessionFor(principal, roles)`. Holding no role in one project says nothing
about another. Where several groups match, the strongest role wins.

Headers presented by an untrusted peer are ignored. The `dev` provider refuses any non-loopback bind.

items.title: server/paths — path confinement
items.body:
Client paths are relative to the project root. Absolute paths, `..` segments, null bytes and drive
letters are refused rather than reinterpreted, because silently serving a reinterpreted path conceals
the caller's bug.

The staged diff is re-checked before a commit is made.

Sparse-checkout is the second defence: the working tree cannot contain application source, so a
path-handling error has nothing dangerous within reach.

items.title: server/git — git plumbing
items.body:
Git commands behind an injectable runner. `run` throws on failure; `tryRun` returns a result,
because "the file does not exist at this ref" is an ordinary answer.

Never force-pushes.

During a rebase, git's index stages are inverted relative to the user's mental model: stage 2 is the
upstream branch and stage 3 is the commit being replayed. `conflictedFile` returns them as the user
means them.

items.title: server/repository — clone and worktrees
items.body:
One bare clone per project and one sparse worktree per user, under `workDir/projects/<id>/`.
Provisioning is serialized, so concurrent requests cannot race one worktree, and lazy, so a user who
never opens a project costs nothing.

`reapIdle(now, idleTimeout)` removes working copies idle beyond the timeout. Two are never removed:

- one holding **uncommitted changes**, which exist in no git object;
- one the process has **not seen used**, so a restart cannot delete drafts. Such a copy is recorded as
  used now and becomes eligible one timeout later.

A reaped copy is re-provisioned on next use.

items.title: server/workingCopy — reads, writes, publication
items.body:
Reads, writes and publication for one user's working copy.

`pendingDiff` reports changes at item level, so the Commit dialog can name `REQ-14` rather than a
filename. `publish` runs: stage → gate → commit as the authenticated user → rebase → retry up to
`pushRetries` → push.

A refused commit returns an outcome describing the refusal; it does not throw, because the refusal is
data the dialog renders. Rebase conflicts in a register document are resolved by `mergeDocs`. Nothing
is force-pushed, and no document is written containing conflict markers.

items.title: server/commitGate — validate and govern before publishing
items.body:
`checkCommit` decides whether a change may enter the repository: structural validity, governance, and
an active job when the policy requires one. Pure over the changed documents plus policy.

Governance runs here rather than in the browser because the client is not trusted. `requireGovernanceClean`
selects `block`, `warn` or `off`.

items.title: server/api — the HTTP surface
items.body:
The HTTP endpoint set: session, documents, status, document and text read/write, commit, discard,
presence.

Authorization is enforced here. The editor's read-only rendering is a courtesy; a reader's write
request is refused server-side regardless of what the client displayed.

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| Path outside the allowlist | 400 |
| Document absent | 404 |
| Write built on a superseded version | 409, carrying the current version |
| Role lacks the capability | 403 |
| Unknown endpoint | 404, naming method and path |

items.title: server entry point — process and static serving
items.body:
One process serving the version-pinned editor build and the API from a single origin. Same origin
removes CORS, third-party cookies, cross-domain redirects, and any dependency on specpad.com being
reachable from inside a corporate network.

An invalid configuration exits non-zero with every problem listed, having listened on nothing.

Shutdown ends the open event streams before closing the server. An SSE stream does not end on its own,
so `close()` alone waits indefinitely and the process must be killed.

Static paths are confined to the build directory; unknown paths fall back to the SPA index.

items.title: server/presence, events, branchWatcher — advisory signals
items.body:
Advisory signals, none of which anything blocks on.

Presence claims expire 45 seconds after their last heartbeat. A heartbeat repeating an existing claim
is not re-broadcast. Losing the registry to a restart costs a period of silence.

The branch watcher polls `ls-remote`. A first observation is not a change, and an unreachable remote
is not a change; either would tell every open editor to reload for nothing.

Events are scoped per project. Dead subscribers are dropped rather than thrown; a malformed frame is
ignored.

items.title: The skill — procedures as a prompt
items.body:
The skill is prose, not a program: an agent procedure with no CLI.

It mirrors the contract in words — the same governance rule ids, file conventions and id discipline —
and `skill/__tests__/parity.test.ts` holds it to the shared module.

Contains the working loop, `init`, the baseline generator, the requirement audit, change-tracking
cache maintenance, the release-cut procedure, and verification-run capture. Authoring guidance for each
document type is in `guides/`, read just-in-time rather than inlined, and `guides.test.ts` keeps the
routing in sync.

items.title: Templates and the pre-push hook
items.body:
Scaffolding for a new project, and the enforcement backstop.

The launcher template hardcodes no editor host. The skill substitutes the base URL and the optional
server project id in both the redirect and the no-JavaScript fallback link; the fallback is what a
blocked-script user sees, so a launcher correct in one place and wrong in the other is worse than one
consistently wrong.

The pre-push hook blocks a commit with no `Job:` trailer and warns on code without spec. It skips
merges, tag pushes and pre-adoption history, and provides a waiver and a bypass — a gate with no escape
hatch is disabled entirely.

`stale-design.mjs`, called by the hook per commit, reports design that may no longer describe the
code. It reads each section's `source` paths from the detailed design **as it stood at that commit**,
and names any changed file whose claiming section is itself unchanged. It reports and never decides:
whether the design actually moved is the author's judgement, so this warns rather than blocks. Without
node, or without a detailed design, it is silent.

items.title: Verification adapter and tooling
items.body:
`specpad-verify.mjs` converts one runner's machine report into the normalized run record. The core
parses no test framework, so another runner is a sibling adapter.

`sync-skill.mjs` mirrors the distributable skill into `.claude/skills/` so this repository runs the
skill it ships. The mirror is committed and checked on push.

items.title: Marketing site and generated reference
items.body:
The marketing site is a second Vite build deployed to the apex; the editor is deployed under its
version path.

The schema reference is generated from the live contract at build time, so it cannot describe a version
of the schema that does not exist.
